PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. — PROJECT LATTICE
ESCALATION MEMORANDUM TO THE TRELLIS SPECIAL COMMITTEE

Re: Second-Turn Markup of SPA Article VIII (Indemnification) by Wexler Bright LLP (Counsel to Halberd Holdings LP) — Escalation of Items Exceeding Deal Team Delegated Authority

Date: (Transmitted with this file under Trellis naming conventions)

To: The Special Committee, Trellis BioWorks, Inc.
From: Trellis Deal Team / Project Lattice Counsel
Subject: Halberd second-turn indemnification markup — comparison to v4, deal team fallbacks, quantifications, and request for approval

This memorandum, filed under Trellis naming conventions in the Trellis matter workspace, escalates for Special Committee approval the five changes Halberd's outside counsel (Wexler Bright LLP) proposed to Article VIII (Indemnification) of the Share Purchase Agreement in its second-turn markup transmitted 30 July 2026 against the Trellis execution draft v4 (the "v4 Draft"). Each change is compared below against (i) the v4 Draft, (ii) the Trellis deal team's Transaction Committee-approved fallback positions (the "Approved Positions," approved 24 July 2026), and (iii) the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14. All dollar figures are derived solely from the source documents, and all cap, basket, and special-indemnity deltas are stated against the Purchase Price of $120,000,000 set forth in the v4 Draft.

I. MARKUP CHANGE BY MARKUP CHANGE ANALYSIS

Change 1 — Section 8.1 (Survival of general representations): 18 months → 36 months.
• v4 Draft position: General representations other than Fundamental Representations survive eighteen (18) months after Closing. Fundamental Representations survive six (6) years; Section 3.16 (Taxes) survival is unchanged; covenants per their terms.
• Halberd ask: Thirty-six (36) months for the general representations (Fundamental and tax survival unchanged).
• Deal team Approved Position (IP-1): Opening position 18 months; approved fallback is a maximum of twenty-four (24) months. A 36-month survival period is expressly "out of policy."
• Assessment: The 36-month ask exceeds the deal team's 24-month fallback by twelve (12) months. This is a material extension of post-closing exposure that the deal team was not delegated authority to grant. EXCEEDS DELEGATED AUTHORITY.

Change 2 — Section 8.3(a) (Basket): true deductible of $400,000 → tipping basket of $250,000.
• v4 Draft position: A true (deductible-threshold) basket of $400,000; the Sellers are liable only for Losses in excess of the $400,000 threshold.
• Halberd ask: Convert to a "tipping" basket of $250,000, under which once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000 the Sellers become liable from the first dollar.
• Deal team Approved Position (IP-3): The basket must remain a true deductible; conversion to a tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold. The deductible may be reduced below $400,000 but not below a floor of $300,000.
• Assessment: Halberd's ask converts the basket to a tipping structure, which the deal team has identified as out of policy at any threshold, and it also drops the threshold to $250,000 — below the $300,000 true-deductible floor. Both the structure (tipping) and the threshold ($250,000) exceed the Approved Position. EXCEEDS DELEGATED AUTHORITY. (For completeness, the deal team's own authorized concession is a true deductible reduced to a $300,000 floor).

Change 3 — Section 8.3(b) (Indemnity cap): 10% ($12,000,000) → 25% ($30,000,000).
• v4 Draft position: Aggregate Sellers' liability under Section 8.2(a) capped at ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price = $12,000,000; Fundamental Representation Losses capped at the Purchase Price ($120,000,000).
• Halberd ask: Increase the general cap to twenty-five percent (25%) of the Purchase Price = $30,000,000 (Fundamental Representations stay capped at the Purchase Price).
• Deal team Approved Position (IP-2): Opening position 10% ($12,000,000); approved fallback is a maximum of fifteen percent (15%) = $18,000,000. A 25% cap is out of policy.
• Quantified cap deltas against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price:
   - v4 → Halberd ask: $30,000,000 − $12,000,000 = +$18,000,000 of additional sellers' exposure.
   - v4 → deal team fallback (15%): $18,000,000 − $12,000,000 = +$6,000,000.
   - Amount of Halberd's ask beyond the deal team's delegated authority: $30,000,000 − $18,000,000 = +$12,000,000 in excess of the approved 15% ($18M) fallback.
• Assessment: The 25% / $30,000,000 cap is twelve million dollars ($12,000,000) above the deal team's approved 15% / $18,000,000 fallback and is out of policy. EXCEEDS DELEGATED AUTHORITY.

Change 4 — NEW Section 8.2(d) (Special Indemnity for Schedule 3.14 matters).
• v4 Draft position: Section 8.2 identifies three indemnifiable categories (breach of representations, breach of covenants, Pre-Closing Taxes) and expressly states that "Execution draft v4 contains no special indemnities."
• Halberd ask: Add a special indemnity under which the Sellers indemnify Buyer for "any and all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14," which indemnity is NOT subject to the Deductible or the Section 8.3 cap and survives until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation.
• Deal team Approved Position (IP-4): A special indemnity for disclosed matters is acceptable ONLY if ALL of the following hold: (i) scope limited to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2 (the pending matters); (ii) an aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of twenty-four (24) months from Closing; and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — are expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.
• Schedule 3.14 items the proposed special indemnity would cover:
   - Item 1 (pending): TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, opposing registration of the TRELLIGEN mark. No damages claimed; exposure is potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding.
   - Item 2 (pending): written demand from Bexley Clinical Partners LLC claiming $1,850,000 in alleged assay-lot-failure damages under the 2024 Supply Agreement (pre-litigation; no suit filed; liability denied; carrier reserved).
   - Item 3 (RESOLVED): OSHA Citation No. 1829445, penalty of $46,500 paid in full and abatement certified; closed resolved matter, disclosed for completeness only.
• Divergences from the Approved Position: The Halberd special indemnity (a) sweeps in Item 3, a resolved matter that the Approved Position expressly requires be excluded; (b) is UNCAPPED (not subject to the Section 8.3 cap) rather than capped at the Approved $2,500,000; and (c) survives until expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation rather than the Approved 24 months from Closing. The proposal is therefore out of policy on scope, cap, and duration.
• Assessment: The Halberd special-indemnity ask exceeds delegated authority on three separate grounds (scope includes a resolved matter; no cap; indefinite survival). EXCEEDS DELEGATED AUTHORITY.

Change 5 — Section 8.5 (Order of Recovery): conforming change for special-indemnity claims.
• v4 Draft position: Buyer recovers first from the Escrow Amount and thereafter severally from the Sellers in proportion to their Pro Rata Shares.
• Halberd ask: Special-indemnity claims are recoverable directly from the Sellers without first exhausting the Escrow Amount.
• Deal team Approved Position: No separate Approved Position addresses order of recovery; this change is purely conforming to the special indemnity proposed in Change 4.
• Assessment: Acceptable only if and to the extent the Special Committee authorizes a special indemnity consistent with the Approved Position. This conforming change does not itself raise an independent dollar delta.

II. QUANTIFICATION SUMMARY (VS. $120,000,000 PURCHASE PRICE)

| Provision | v4 Draft | Halberd Ask | Deal Team Approved Fallback | $ Delta v4 → Ask | Exceeds Delegated Authority? |
|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| Survival (8.1) | 18 months | 36 months | max 24 months | — (term, not $) | Yes |
| Basket (8.3(a)) | true deductible $400,000 | tipping basket $250,000 | true deductible, floor $300,000 | — (structure + $150,000) | Yes |
| Cap (8.3(b)) | $12,000,000 (10%) | $30,000,000 (25%) | $18,000,000 (15%) | +$18,000,000 | Yes (+$12,000,000 above fallback) |
| Special Indemnity (8.2(d)) | none | uncapped; all of Schedule 3.14; to statute limitations | cap $2,500,000; Items 1–2 only; 24 months | — (uncapped) | Yes |
| Order of Recovery (8.5) | Escrow-first | special-indemnity direct | conforming | — | Contingent on Change 4 |

III. RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVAL REQUEST

Every one of Halberd's five proposed changes exceeds the deal team's Transaction Committee-approved delegated authority, and none can be accepted by the deal team without Special Committee approval. Two of the changes (cap, survival) are direct numerical increases beyond approved fallbacks; the basket change converts the structure to a tipping basket that is out of policy at any threshold; and the special indemnity, by sweeping in the resolved OSHA matter, being uncapped, and running to the statute of limitations, violates all four of the Approved Position's preconditions.

We recommend that the Special Committee authorize the deal team to respond to Wexler Bright as follows:
1. Survival (Change 1): reject 36 months; counter at the approved 24-month fallback.
2. Basket (Change 2): reject the tipping basket; if concession is warranted on this point, offer a true deductible reduced to the $300,000 floor (not below), preserving the true-deductible structure.
3. Cap (Change 3): reject 25%; the deal team may move from 10% to the approved 15% / $18,000,000 fallback but no further.
4. Special Indemnity (Change 4): the special indemnity may be offered ONLY in the form authorized by the Approved Position — limited to pending Schedule 3.14 Items 1 and 2, capped at an aggregate of $2,500,000, surviving 24 months from Closing, and expressly excluding resolved Item 3 (the OSHA matter).
5. Order of Recovery (Change 5): conform to the special indemnity only if and as authorized; otherwise revert to the v4 Escrow-first/default pro-rata order.

Because the requested cap ($30,000,000) exceeds the deal team's approved 15% by $12,000,000, and because a 36-month survival, a tipping basket, and an uncapped indefinite special indemnity are each out of policy, the deal team has no authority to concede these items absent express Special Committee approval. We respectfully request that the Special Committee (a) approve the responsive positions set out above, or (b) provide such greater or lesser authority as the Committee deems appropriate. Given Wexler Bright's cover note indicating its investment-committee mandate and its request for a responsive special-indemnity rider, an expedited decision is requested.
